A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Orthogonal Residual Update work. All 34 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison; the appendices are textually and visually unchanged.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-classification experiments, training measurements and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with one revised classification result in Table 2.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix G retain the same projection-based residual update, feature-wise and global variants, algorithm and PyTorch implementations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet and ImageNet-1k. The appendix experiments retain the same data and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments, including linear residual baselines, learned stream scaling and the unified residual family in Appendix E.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same architectures, data splits, preprocessing, training budgets and evaluation procedures. Neither PDF reports a setting change associated with the revised Table 2 result.

E4.justification: The learning-rate, connection-switching, probability, layer-pattern and epsilon analyses are unchanged. Appendices C–E retain identical initialization, final-LayerNorm, internal-dynamics and residual-family analyses.

E5.justification: Table 2 still reports mean and standard deviation over five runs, averaging the five best validation epochs within each run. Other run counts, error bars, interquartile bands and correlation tests are unchanged. One changed standard-deviation value belongs to E6.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes ViT-B Orthogonal-F CIFAR-10 validation Acc@1 from 88.73 ± 6.06% to 91.93 ± 0.08%; its Linear comparator remains 87.28 ± 0.41%. This is a localized numerical revision under unchanged reported settings. All other results, including appendix tables and plots, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, update equations, Appendix B derivations and Appendix F width-to-depth ratio analysis are unchanged. The stream-scaling argument moves partly between pages 6 and 5 without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about generalization, training stability and efficiency. The highlighted ViT-B ImageNet-1k improvement remains +3.78 percentage points.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 replaces reviewer-directed wording with a direct statement that parallel suppression occurs under linear residual updates, preserving the existing interpretation. Mechanism explanations, applicability qualifications and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures; Appendix G retains identical implementation code. The code/model access statement is unchanged, and no technical explanation accompanies the revised Table 2 estimate.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the reference list are unchanged. The distinction between modifying the skip pathway and projecting the additive update retains the same research positioning.

P1.justification: v5 shortens one sentence in Section 3.4 to remove reference to a reviewer's request, revises the funding acknowledgement to include an additional grant, and updates the version/date header. Section organization and appendix prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened sentence causes localized text reflow on pages 5–6, moving one line of the stream-scaling argument onto page 5. Figures, table structures, captions, axes and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 provides a small editorial cleanup, but its substantive revision is the unexplained replacement of Table 2's ViT-B CIFAR-10 estimate with a higher mean and much smaller standard deviation. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects an error or reflects recomputed results, so improved evidential reliability cannot be inferred. With methods, analyses and appendices otherwise unchanged, a net quality improvement is uncertain.
